speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me your age and when you experienced your first menstrual period? Also, have you had any unexplained fractures or bone pain in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did your mother experience hirsutism or acne during her pregnancy, and have you noticed any darkening of the skin, particularly in body folds or on the back of your neck? I also need to know if you have any history of hearing loss or vision problems.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Delayed menarche. I also have Severe acne, History of fractures following minor trauma, Partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly noted at birth.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Karyotype
REQUEST TEST: Serum 17-OH Progesterone

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal karyotype and 17-OH progesterone, these findings rule out classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia and Turner syndrome. Could you describe your height relative to your peers, and have you noticed any excessive hair growth on your face or body?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Currently taking oral isotretinoin for acne and an oral contraceptive. Social history: The patient is a high school student without significant tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a family history of early puberty or bone fractures? I need to check for signs of aromatase deficiency. REQUEST TEST: LH and FSH levels

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal LH and FSH levels, aromatase deficiency is less likely, so I need to evaluate for other causes of androgen excess and bone fragility. Do you have a history of short stature or tall stature, and have you noticed any excessive hair growth on your face or body?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies any recent illnesses, appetite change, or weight change.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned your mother had chin hair during pregnancy; did she also have signs of virilization or hirsutism throughout her life? I need to determine if this is a familial androgen excess disorder.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies any recent illnesses, appetite change, or weight change.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of virilization at birth, bone fragility, and primary amenorrhea with normal gonadotropins strongly suggests a disorder of steroidogenesis. REQUEST TEST: Serum Testosterone, DHEAS, and Bone Density Scan

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated androgens combined with osteoporosis and virilization at birth point toward aromatase deficiency, despite the normal LH/FSH. I need to confirm the estrogen status to distinguish this from other causes of androgen excess. REQUEST TEST: Serum Estradiol

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of virilization at birth, primary amenorrhea, elevated androgens, low estradiol, and severe osteoporosis is diagnostic of aromatase deficiency, as the body cannot convert androgens to estrogens. DIAGNOSIS READY: Aromatase Deficiency
